title: KV cache tiered-precision evaluation: INT8 vs FP8 trade-offs for latency and quality
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket covers an empirical evaluation and calibration workflow for applying reduced-precision formats to the KV cache. We compared INT8 and FP8 encodings across representative request mixes (chat prefixes, long-context retrieval, and batched inference) to measure latency variance, steady-state throughput, and generation quality regression. The goal is to produce an operational recommendation and an automated calibration pipeline (dataset + percentiles) that can be used by runtime to select a default KV quantization profile and runtime fallback policy.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook describing calibration dataset, collector config, and percentile/clipping strategy published to Confluence
Quantized-kv runtime mode(s) implemented behind feature flag with telemetry for per-request quant-format and cache-hit precision
Quality regression on eval-suite-v2 kept within defined thresholds (<= 1.0% mean task delta, <= 0.5% for sensitive tasks)
Performance dashboard showing P50/P95/P99 latency and token throughput across INT8, FP8, and FP16 baseline for seq_len 512/2048/4096
Automated CI calibration job that emits recommended layer-wise scaling factors (CSV) and stores artifacts in S3
steps: Define representative calibration corpora: prefix-heavy chat (10k prompts), retrieval-primed longform (3k docs), QA/eval-suite-v2 (5k prompts)
Implement histogram-based collector in serving runtime to gather activation ranges per-layer/head for cached KV tensors
Run offline calibration sweeps: max-abs clipping, 99.999 percentile clipping, MSE-minimizing per-layer scale for INT8 and FP8
Quantize cached KV tensors using chosen scheme and run batched microbenchmarks across target hardware (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and Ampere L4) to measure latency/throughput
Execute automated quality evals (synthetic and human-in-the-loop sampling) and capture metric deltas vs FP16 baseline
Iterate on asymmetric per-head scaling for top-attention heads where divergence observed; test tiered precision (FP8 for high-signal heads, INT8 elsewhere)
Document results, propose default policy, and create rollout plan with canary thresholds
results_summary: Baseline: FP16 cached-KV runtime used as quality/latency reference
INT8 (symmetric per-layer) produced best steady-state throughput at high concurrency but introduced occasional outlier token substitutions in long-context summarization tasks
FP8 (8-bit floating) retained more of the dynamic range and showed smaller quality regressions while still reducing memory bandwidth relative to FP16
Tiered policy (FP8 for top-k attention heads, INT8 for remainder) offers a middle ground: ~75% of INT8 throughput gains with quality close to FP8 on evaluated prompts
perf_numbers: INT8 P95 latency: 52ms (+13% vs FP16), P99 tail spikes up to +30% under cold-cache churn
FP8 P95 latency: 48ms (+4% vs FP16), P99 tail +9%
Tiered FP8/INT8 P95 latency: 49ms (+6.5% vs FP16), P99 tail +12%
Throughput (tokens/s) on A100-80GB: FP16 120k, FP8 160k (+33%), INT8 180k (+50%), Tiered 150k (+25%)
quality_metrics: Eval-suite-v2 mean task delta (higher means worse): INT8 +0.9%, FP8 +0.25%, Tiered +0.35%
Long-context summarization rouge-L delta: INT8 -1.5 points, FP8 -0.4 points, Tiered -0.6 points
Log-prob token divergence (mean KL over tokens): INT8 0.018, FP8 0.005, Tiered 0.006
Human rating (n=300 pairwise): INT8 preferred 28% vs FP16, FP8 preferred 46% vs FP16, Tiered preferred 42%
tradeoffs: INT8: strongest memory and bandwidth savings; higher latency variance and occasional quality cliff for long-contexts and specific attention heads
FP8: smoother quality retention with moderate memory savings; requires careful exponent-bias handling and slightly more compute for conversion
Tiered: operational complexity increases (need per-head profiling/metadata, more knobs), but gives best cost/quality balance in many workloads
Calibration dataset mismatch risk: using synthetic short prompts underestimates extremes seen in customer retrieval chains leading to unobserved regressions
decisions: Adopt a conservative default: FP8 KV cache for hosted runtime in runtime-1.26 with feature flag gated INT8-only aggressive mode for dedicated customers
Implement tiered precision as an opt-in optimization behind controlled rollout (canary followed by staged ramp) rather than default
Calibration pipeline will use percentile clipping at 99.999 for INT8 and per-layer exponent search for FP8 as the baseline algorithms
Add per-request telemetry to capture 'quant-format', 'cache-warmth', 'seq_len', and 'top-10 attention head divergences' to aid future tuning
blockers: Histogram collector currently adds 8-12% CPU overhead on hot path; need an async sampling variant before enabling in-hosted default
Ambiguity in hardware FP8 semantics across vendor kernels (oneAPI vs cuDNN FP8 paths produce slightly different encodings) — coordination with low-level kernel team required
Need legal/PR review for storing per-head profile artifacts that may include derived stats from customer prompts (privacy review queued)
next_steps: Prototype async histogram sampler (Marco) - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1234
Kernel alignment sync with infra/kernels team to reconcile FP8 encoding differences (meeting scheduled 2026-03-08)
Create canary rollout plan in Console: define metric thresholds for quality/regression and automated rollback on regression > 1%
Run extended 72-hour soak on canary cluster with diverse customer traces to validate tail behavior
